short: No bigeodesics in planar first passage

title.title: Planar first-passage percolation has no bigeodesics
title.subtitle: Claim: with iid random edge times on $\mathbb Z^2$, no doubly infinite fastest route exists, almost surely

plain: Random travel times on a city grid: can a single fastest route run forever in both directions?

steps: Suppose a fastest route runs forever in both directions
Busemann functions trap its two ends inside narrow sectors
A budget of labels on each horizontal line runs out: impossible

voice.text: Give every street a random travel time. Could one fastest route run forever in both directions?
Assume one exists; trap its ends, and a label budget runs out.
